housing: Rochford is a commuter district between Southend and the Essex countryside, mostly owner-occupied, with one of the lowest private renting shares in Essex. Rayleigh, Hockley and Hawkwell are dominated by post-war semis, bungalows and chalet bungalows, while Rochford town has an older Georgian and Victorian centre. Large new-build estates have been added around Rayleigh and Rochford. Hullbridge and the riverside and estuary villages include bungalows and homes on low-lying land near the River Crouch and the marshes.
checkinTips: Bungalows and chalet bungalows in Hockley, Hawkwell and Ashingdon: photograph loft rooms, dormer windows, flat-roof extensions and gardens.
Riverside homes in Hullbridge and near the Crouch: photograph any damp low on walls, air bricks and signs of past flooding.
Period buildings in Rochford's old town: record sash windows, old doors and floors, and any damp.
New-build estates around Rayleigh and Rochford: note snagging marks, sealant, parking spaces and new fences and turf.
Homes under the Southend Airport flight path: note window and door seals and any trickle vents.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Rochford District Council's private sector housing team.
